From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 7 May 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: token volumes & rough unit economics

Hi Priya — thanks again for the call today. Short recap and next steps so we’re aligned: 

- What we heard you say: 1) Proof-of-concept (P0) for the recommender/proactive insights use case will start with ~3M user-triggered requests/month, avg prompt+response length ~250 tokens. 2) Expected growth to ~30–40M requests/month in 12 months if P0 meets accuracy targets. 3) Security: SOC2 evidence requested, but you already have an NDA in place.

Quick back-of-envelope unit economics we sketched on-screen (please confirm):
- Baseline model (mixed open LLM): ~0.8–1.2M tokens per $1 external cost (target: $/1M tokens between $800–$1,200) depending on batching and cache hit rate.
- With KV caching and 50% prefix reuse we expect effective cost to improve ~25–35%.

Ask / next steps: 
1) Can you confirm monthly active request volumes by environment (P0, staging, prod) — rough buckets are fine.
2) Would Procurement prefer a 12-month reserved capacity estimate or month-to-month hosted with a committed spend band?
3) I’ll send an initial pro forma (pricing_model_v3.xlsx) showing tiered per-token bands and an illustrative invoice. If numbers look good, Ben (cc’d) will pull finance-ready terms and an invoice draft.

Attaching meeting notes and the initial calculator (will send in follow-up email).

Thanks,
Connor O'Brien

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: token volumes & rough unit economics

Connor — thanks for the clear notes. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Volumes: P0 (Q3 pilot) ~3M requests/mo as you noted; expected prod ramp 18–24 months to 50–60M requests/mo if P0 success criteria met. Average tokens per request is likely closer to 300 tokens total (prompt+response) once we include longer context for personalization.
- Traffic shape: we have strong diurnal peaks (30% of daily traffic in a 2-hr window). Latency SLO is important — cannot exceed 400ms p50 for interactive features.
- Budget: procurement gave a preliminary annual budget range of $250k–$600k for the first year depending on negotiated unit price and whether reserved capacity or committed discounts are applied.

Questions for you: can the pro forma show both: 1) hosted consumption pricing with estimated monthly invoices, and 2) a 12-month reserved commitment scenario with committed-rate $/1M tokens and predictability on latency SLOs? Also please call out assumptions (batching levels, KV cache hit %, avg seq length) used to produce the unit pricing.

Happy to jump on a quick 20-min call Monday to walk through the spreadsheet.

—Priya

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Priya Singh <priya@astercloud.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 9 May 2026 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Draft invoice / committed scenario request

Priya — looping in finance as requested. Connor shared estimated budget range; per our internal pricing playbook I sketched two scenarios that map to your $250k–$600k guidance: 

1) Hosted consumption (no commit) — conservative estimate at projected 12-month avg of 20M req/month, 300 tokens/request -> ~6B tokens/month. Using tiered pricing and typical batching/caching assumptions (20% cache, small batching boost) results in an illustrative $/1M tokens = $1,050. That maps to ~$6,300/month per 1B tokens -> total annualized spend roughly $75k–$200k depending on growth curve.

2) 12-month Reserved (committed capacity) — with a 30% commit discount and guaranteed latency SLOs, target $/1M tokens can drop to ~$735 in our model. With the same traffic profile that gives you predictable monthly billing and headroom for burst. We included a three-tier commitment bracket (small/medium/large) in the attached pro forma.

I attached a quick invoice_estimate_AST-4721.pdf that pulls numbers from the spreadsheet; Connor will send the source spreadsheet for your review. 

Ben Carter
Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>

Date: Sat, 9 May 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Unit economics pro forma + attachments (pricing_model_v3.xlsx)

Priya — attaching the spreadsheet and a quick invoice PDF (attachments listed below). Summary of what changed since Ben's note: 

- Updated avg tokens/request to 300 across all scenarios.
- Added explicit rows for batching assumptions: small-batch (10–20 reqs), large-batch (50–150 reqs) and an estimated effective speed-up for our runtime.
- Cache scenarios: 0%, 25%, 50% prefix reuse. Pipeline-level savings are shown separately from raw model unit price.
- Committed tiers: bronze/silver/gold with stepped discounts and included burst capacity.

Topline recommendation (for alignment with your budget band):
- If you plan to keep annual spend < $300k, hosted consumption with moderate batching and a 20% caching hit is likely the simplest path. 
- If you expect sustained > $400k annual spend and want predictability, a 12-month reserved commit (silver tier) looks most cost-efficient — target $/1M tokens ~$750 in our model.

Please review the attached pricing_model_v3.xlsx and the invoice_estimate_AST-4721.pdf. If this looks reasonable, can we lock a 20-min review Monday 10:00am PT? Happy to adjust assumptions live and export a procurement-ready estimate.

Thanks again,
